kitDescription: Mint is a Burst II rocket-launcher supporter built around a two-stance 'Assigned Part' cycle. Every time she casts her burst she flips stance — her first burst puts her in Dancing, the next in Singing, and so on — and the stance sticks until the next burst flips it. Her burst always gives the whole team a 10-second 'Sing Along' package regardless of stance: +30.02% Attack Damage, +40% Max Ammunition Capacity and +45.05% Critical Damage. While she is in Singing, each full-charge rocket she fires gives all allies a 3-second ATK boost worth 45.02% of Mint's own ATK, and whenever the team reaches Burst Stage 3 she adds 19.94% Critical Rate, 50% Projectile Explosion Damage and 32.72% Pierce Damage to the team for 10 seconds. While she is in Dancing instead, those same charged shots heal the team for 1.8% of her Max HP every second for 3 seconds. She deals no skill or burst damage of her own — everything she contributes to a team's output is buffing.

redAssertions: M1 'is GATED on Assigned Part: Singing — does NOT fire on every shot': driver fires the (halved) casterAtkPct on every charged shot of the fight, so applications == shots, not < shots.
M4/M5/M6 'is GATED on Singing — does NOT fire on every stage-3 entry': driver applies the (halved) trio at every stage-3 entry, so frames == stage3Frames, not < stage3Frames.
M4/M5/M6 magnitude assertions (critRatePct 19.94 / projectileExplosionPct 50 / pierceDamagePct 32.72): driver ships 9.97 / 25 / 16.36 in the default solo mode.
M1 magnitude-derived flat value (0.4502 x mint.staticAtk): driver ships 0.2251 x staticAtk in solo.
M2 'a recovery consumer is reached at all' and 'is a 3-TICK heal-over-time': driver drops the Dancing heal entirely, so no recovery event exists.
M7 'Singing and Dancing produce isolated windows': driver has no Dancing branch, so the Dancing-side observable never appears.

skill1.driverSaid: shotFired → allies, casterAtkPct, durationSec 3; value 22.51 in default 'solo' (kit-literal 45.02 halved as a 50%-duty-cycle proxy), 45.02 in 'duet (w/ Prika)'.
skill1.blindSaid: S2b + S5 + S6 all agree on stat casterAtkPct (flat = pct x caster ATK, never atkPct), trigger shotFired, target allies, 3s. S2b/S5 demand a dynamic Singing gate at kit-literal 45.02; S6 freezes a static 'singing' mode at 45.02 and admits in its own caveats that this over-credits ~2x.
skill1.formulaCheck: casterAtkPct resolves to a FLAT ATK add in the ATK term (damage-calculation.md), and damage is LINEAR in ATK — so a 50% duty cycle at full value and 100% duty cycle at half value are identical in expectation. The proxy's only error term is covariance between teammate damage and the Singing windows, plus duty-cycle arithmetic (see gotcha 1).
skill1.explanation: Stat identity, caster-scaling, target set, duration and per-full-charge cadence are corroborated GREEN by the S5 blind run (17 passes include exactly these). The only divergence is the mechanism/magnitude proxy, which the driver's note flags as ⚑ residual 1 with estimate ('a few % at board level'), recipe (Mint-focus recording comparing Singing-window vs Dancing-window team damage) and tier (2). Separately, the 'Full Charge' → shotFired reduction is convergent across all three models but is the ONE assumption the driver did not record in its note (S6 did) — see gotcha 3.

skill1.driverSaid: Listed verbatim-ish under unmodeled.skill1 with a ⚑ in the note: defensive, engine has no HP pool, only damage channel is a Crown-style on-recovery consumer (owner finding F1: 'crown recovery consumer never procs'); estimate small, recipe = wire heal ticks:3 intervalSec:1 Dancing-gated and measure the consumer's uplift, tier 2.

skill1.formulaCheck: No HP pool in engine v1, so the heal has no direct damage path; the only route to damage is a teammate's on-recovery trigger. Note that S6's encoding is functionally equivalent to the driver's in the DEFAULT mode — neither ships a live recovery emitter out of the box.

The residual cold bias is real but bounded to comps carrying a recovery consumer, and it is a known repo-wide bias (F1), not a mint-specific fabrication. Ranked below gotcha 1.

gotchas.summary: The Assigned-Part duty cycle is modeled as a static value-HALVING proxy firing every rotation, not as a dynamic part-state gate at kit-literal magnitudes — so the shipped solo values (22.51 / 9.97 / 25 / 16.36) differ from the prose's own numbers (45.02 / 19.94 / 50 / 32.72), and the driver's justifying premise that no engine primitive expresses the flip is contradicted by two independent blinds.
gotchas.evidence: Kit prose: burst 'Status 2: If not in the Assigned Part: Dancing status, Mint gains Assigned Part: Dancing' then 'Status 1: ... gains Assigned Part: Singing' = strict alternation from a no-part start, so burst 1 leaves her DANCING and the Singing-side output is absent in rotation 1 and live on even rotations only. Formula (damage-calculation.md): the three affected channels are all LINEAR in the buffed quantity — casterAtkPct is a flat ATK add in a linear term, projectileExplosionPct is additive inside the Damage Up bucket, and expected damage is linear in crit rate (1 + rate x (critDmg - 1)) — therefore halving the value at 100% uptime is EXACT in expectation for a true 50% duty cycle. This is why the proxy is a legitimate approximation and not a fudge. Two residual error terms remain: (i) covariance between teammate damage and the Singing windows (the driver's own flagged ⚑), and (ii) duty-cycle arithmetic — over a 180s fight with an ODD number of Mint casts the Singing share is (floor(n/2))/n, e.g. 4/9 ≈ 44%, so a flat 0.5 factor slightly OVER-credits (~13% relative on those four lines). Driver vs blind: S6 (opus) converged on the mode approach and conceded its own static 'singing' mode over-credits ~2x, i.e. WORSE than the driver's proxy; but S2b (fable) and S5 (opus) INDEPENDENTLY and identically claim the alternation is expressible today — 'a resource pool driven by two burstCast blocks with everyN:2 / everyNOffset 0|1, read back by resourceGate on the S1 and S2 blocks'. That cross-family agreement on a specific primitive path directly contradicts the driver's note ('no self-buff-active gate' / 'the engine has no dynamic-status primitive') and is the load-bearing premise the owner must re-check.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Do NOT change any magnitude to hit a board number. Step 1 (free, no measurement): verify against the effect schema whether resource / resourceGate / everyN / everyNOffset compose as S2b and S5 both claim. If they DO, the faithful encoding is available today — drive a part resource from two burstCast blocks (everyN:2, everyNOffset 1 -> Dancing, offset 0 -> Singing) and resourceGate the skill1 Singing block and the skill2 trio on it, restoring the KIT-LITERAL 45.02 / 19.94 / 50 / 32.72; that also reproduces rotation-1 absence and even/odd parity, which the proxy cannot. Re-grade the mint comp afterwards and treat any ratio movement as fit-exposure (the overrides were tuned against the proxy), re-tuning exposed units separately rather than re-fudging. If the primitives do NOT compose, keep the proxy but replace the flat 0.5 with the measured duty cycle floor(n/2)/n from the actual cast count in the graded rotation, and record that arithmetic in the note. ⚑ estimate: a few % at board level from the covariance term plus ~13% relative over-credit on the four gated lines from the 0.5-vs-0.444 duty cycle; recipe: Mint-focus recording comparing Singing-window vs Dancing-window team damage, plus a rotation log to count her casts over 180s; tier 2.

gotchas.summary: The Dancing heal (1.8% of caster Max HP every 1 sec for 3 sec) is dropped entirely, so no recovery event is emitted and any on-recovery consumer in the comp goes unfed.
gotchas.evidence: Kit prose: 'Dancing Effect: Constantly recovers 1.8% of the skill user's final Max HP every 1 sec for 3 sec.' Formula: engine v1 models no HP pool, so the heal has NO direct damage path — its only damage channel is a teammate's on-recovery trigger (owner finding F1, 'crown recovery consumer never procs', is the known repo-wide cold bias). Driver vs blind: S2b rates it FAITHFUL and load-bearing as a recovery-EVENT emitter and S5 writes three assertions against a crown consumer (cluster B, 3 RED); S6 wires it as heal ticks:3 / intervalSec:1 but mode-gates it to 'dancing', so S6's own DEFAULT mode is just as silent as the driver's. Net practical divergence between driver and S6 in default configuration: zero.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Needs the part-state gate first (it shares gotcha 1's blocker): once a Dancing state is expressible, wire the S6 encoding — kind heal, ticks:3, intervalSec:1, target allies, trigger shotFired, gated to Dancing — so recovery consumers are driven on the correct half of the rotations. Do not wire it ungated: an always-on heal would feed a consumer 2x. ⚑ estimate: zero in any comp without a recovery consumer, small-but-nonzero in a crown-carrying comp; recipe: run the S5 HEAL fixture (liter / mint / crown / helm with every OTHER heal stripped) and measure crown's on-recovery attackDamagePct uplift with the heal wired vs dropped; tier 2.

gotchas.summary: 'Activates when attacking with Full Charge' is reduced to a bare shotFired trigger with no recorded assumption — convergent across all three models, but the driver alone never flags it.
gotchas.evidence: Kit prose: 'Activates when attacking with Full Charge' — a charge-completion condition, not a trigger-pull condition. All four artifacts encode it as shotFired on the premise that an RL (chargeFrames 60) fires only fully-charged shots; S6 records this explicitly as a ⚑ ('Any partial-charge shots in the engine's RL path would over-fire this block'), S2b records it in its scope field, and the driver's note does not mention it at all. Because all three models share the premise, convergence here is WEAK evidence — this is same-model agreement, not independent verification.
gotchas.suggestedFix: No encoding change unless the premise is false. Verify that the engine's RL path emits shotFired only on completed charges (and never on a partial/cancelled charge); if it can emit on uncharged shots, gate the block accordingly. Either way, add the one-line assumption to the override note so the reduction is on the record rather than inherited silently. This is a documentation fix, not a magnitude change.

faithfulnessScore: 1.0 (10/10 kit lines FAITHFUL or DOCUMENTED_GAP — 4 FAITHFUL, 6 DOCUMENTED_GAP, 0 REAL-GOTCHA, 0 RECON_ERROR)
verdictRationale: GO. (a) Every damage-relevant line is accounted for at the correct stat, bucket, trigger identity, target set and duration, and no magnitude anywhere is fabricated: 45.02 / 19.94 / 50 / 32.72 / 30.02 / 40 / 45.05 are all kit-literal and all three blinds converge on them exactly. The two hardest identity calls are independently CONFIRMED by S5 running unmodified against the shipped override — the skill2 trio fires on stage-3 ENTRY and never on Mint's own stage-2 cast (she is Burst II, so her own cast could never be the trigger), and the Sing Along trio fires on her burstCast rather than fullBurstEnter, once per cast, mode-invariant. maxAmmoPct 40 and critRatePct are both proven LIVE levers by S5's strip-and-compare tests, satisfying the modeled-≠-working check; no invented stat, no invented damage line (she is correctly a pure supporter). (b) The halving proxy is a legitimate disclosed approximation, not a faithfulness failure. It is arithmetically exact in expectation, because all three gated channels enter damage linearly — a flat ATK add, an additive Damage-Up entry, and crit rate through 1 + rate x (critDmg - 1) — so 50% uptime at full value and 100% uptime at half value are the same number. The blind's static full-value 'singing' mode is strictly WORSE by its own written admission (~2x over-credit), and the owner has validated the proxy at 1.015 on the graded comp. It carries a complete ⚑ (estimate + recipe + tier 2). (c) The Dancing heal's UNMODELED disposition is acceptable — no HP pool exists in v1, the magnitude is genuinely unmodelable, the only channel is an on-recovery consumer, and S6's mode-gated encoding is equally silent in its own default mode. Ranked gotchas: (1) the Singing-gate mechanism, med; (2) the Dancing heal, low; (3) the undocumented Full-Charge → shotFired reduction, low. What the owner should spot-check — and the one place I distrust the packet's framing: the claim that 'all three models agree no engine primitive expresses the dynamic flip' is NOT what the artifacts say. S2b (fable-5) and S5 (opus-5), from different model families and blind to each other, both name the same concrete shipped-primitive path — a part resource driven by two burstCast blocks with everyN:2 / everyNOffset 0|1, read back via resourceGate on the skill1 and skill2 blocks. Only S6 and the driver assert inexpressibility. If those primitives compose as described, the kit-literal dynamic encoding is available TODAY at zero measurement cost, and it would additionally reproduce rotation-1 absence and even/odd parity — which the proxy structurally cannot — as well as fix a second-order error I found independently: with an odd number of Mint casts over 180s the true Singing share is floor(n/2)/n (≈44% at 9 casts), so a flat 0.5 factor over-credits the four gated lines by ~13% relative. That is a schema check, not an experiment, and it is the single highest-value follow-up. It does not block GO, because the shipped encoding contains no fabricated value and every divergence is recorded with estimate, recipe and tier. Residual on my own verdict: I adjudicated from the pasted artifacts and the reported 17/9/1 S5 run without tool access, so the S5 pass/fail counts and the existence of the resource/resourceGate/everyN primitives are both taken from the packet rather than re-executed; I could not write scripts/kit-autonomy/results/mint.json — this JSON is the return value.
